speaker: unhappy
text: I’ve been thinking about how things are going. Honestly? I don’t feel listened to.
variants: I’ve been thinking about how things are going. Honestly? I don’t feel listened to.
Can I be blunt, {title}? Every time it matters, you go the other way. People notice. I notice.
I made a list of the times you overruled me. It started as a short list.

choices.label: Tell me what you’d change.
choices.reaction: {speaker} talks for forty minutes. You listen for all of them. It helps more than either of you expected.

choices.label: Things are fine.
choices.reaction: {speaker} says “fine” back, in a tone that suggests the list will get longer.

speaker: devoted
text: I’d like to take on more. Give me something to run.
variants: I’d like to take on more. Give me something to run.
You can rely on me, {title}. Put me in charge of something. Anything. Ideally something with a clipboard.
I’ve been doing extra on the side anyway. I may as well do it officially.

choices.label: Run a new initiative.
choices.reaction: {speaker} starts that afternoon. By evening there is a sign-up sheet and a sub-initiative.

choices.label: You’re doing plenty already.
choices.reaction: {speaker} nods, slightly deflated, and does it unofficially anyway.

speaker: any
text: On day {pastDay}, when {pastWho} raised it, you decided: “{pastText}.” Not everyone has made peace with that.
variants: On day {pastDay}, when {pastWho} raised it, you decided: “{pastText}.” Not everyone has made peace with that.
People are still talking about day {pastDay}. You said “{pastText}.” Some of them have started quoting it back at each other.
A member asked me whether “{pastText}” is still the rule, or whether it was more of a mood. I didn’t know what to tell her.

choices.label: I stand by it.
choices.reaction: It is reaffirmed. Someone writes it on the wall, slightly bigger than before.

choices.label: Maybe it’s time to revisit it.
choices.reaction: A working group is formed to revisit it. It meets once, has snacks and agrees to meet again.

text: Could I have a pin for perfect attendance? I’ve not missed a {meeting} since spring.
variants: Could I have a pin for perfect attendance? I’ve not missed a {meeting} since spring.
Would it be all right if I brought my mother to the next {meeting}? She has questions. She has a lot of questions.
Some of us work nights. Could there be a second {meeting}, maybe at six in the morning? We’d bring the {beliefNoun}.
I’d like to start a small reading group within the group. It would just be about {belief}. And possibly whales.

choices.label: Of course.
choices.reaction: {ctx.anon} is delighted and tells everyone. Three more people ask for the same thing by Friday.

choices.label: Not right now.
choices.reaction: {ctx.anon} takes it well, in the sense that they only mention it twice afterwards.

text: I joined last week. Where’s the handbook? Who do I ask things? Is the {beliefNoun} mandatory? Nobody will give me a straight answer.
variants: I joined last week. Where’s the handbook? Who do I ask things? Is the {beliefNoun} mandatory? Nobody will give me a straight answer.
Everyone keeps referring to “the garage” as if I should know what happened there. What happened there?
I’ve been told three different things about {day}s by three different people. One of them was Gary.

choices.label: Assign them a mentor.
choices.reaction: The mentor scheme is born. Its first mentee becomes its most enthusiastic mentor within a month.

choices.label: Figure it out like we did.
choices.reaction: {ctx.anon} figures it out, mostly by watching what Gary does and doing the opposite.

text: I live near where your people meet in {city}. The parking is impossible, the singing is constant and someone keeps leaving {beliefNoun} on my wall.
variants: I live near where your people meet in {city}. The parking is impossible, the singing is constant and someone keeps leaving {beliefNoun} on my wall.
Your members in {city} keep complimenting my hedge. I don’t want it complimented. I want it left alone.
My children have started {belief} at breakfast. I did not raise them to do that. Who is responsible for this?

choices.label: Apologize and fix it.
choices.reaction: A sincere apology and a small gift. {ctx.anon} is unconvinced but noticeably softer.

choices.label: We have every right to be here.
choices.reaction: Members cheer. {ctx.anon} writes to the local paper, which prints it under a photograph of the hedge.

text: I’m doing a piece on {movement}. My editor wants to know if it’s true that your members spend their evenings {belief}. Is it?
variants: I’m doing a piece on {movement}. My editor wants to know if it’s true that your members spend their evenings {belief}. Is it?
We’re running a feature: “Who Are the {Members}?” I have two hundred words and one photograph of a pebble. Help me out.
Quick one. A reader says your organization has more committees than members. Comment?

choices.label: Give them the full story.
choices.reaction: The piece runs with a headline that is almost, but not quite, what you said.

choices.label: No comment.
choices.reaction: The piece runs anyway, under the headline “Group Declines to Comment.” Enquiries rise.

speaker: agenda:order
text: We need a sign-in sheet. Not for any sinister reason. Just so we know who was here, when, and why.
variants: We need a sign-in sheet. Not for any sinister reason. Just so we know who was here, when, and why.
I’ve drafted a schedule. It covers chairs, cups, keys and the emotional support of whoever is doing the cups.
Can we agree, formally, on who is allowed to change the thermostat? It has become a matter of faith for some people.

choices.label: Make it official.
choices.reaction: It is laminated by sundown. {speaker} looks more relaxed than anyone has seen them in weeks.

choices.label: Let people sort it out.
choices.reaction: People sort it out, after a fashion. The thermostat changes eleven times on {day}.

speaker: agenda:joy
text: Everyone’s working so hard. Can we just have a party? A small one. With food. Possibly a large one.
variants: Everyone’s working so hard. Can we just have a party? A small one. With food. Possibly a large one.
What if this {day} we didn’t do any business at all, and just enjoyed each other’s company? Like at the start.
I’ve booked a coach for a day out to the seaside. I haven’t told anyone it costs money yet.

choices.label: Yes. We’ve earned it.
choices.reaction: It is, by common agreement, the best evening anyone can remember. Martin takes minutes anyway.

choices.label: After the next milestone.
choices.reaction: The party is postponed. The bunting stays in a box, glaring at people.

speaker: agenda:purity
text: Members have been treating “{tradition}” rather casually. If we don’t hold the line, it will mean nothing.
variants: Members have been treating “{tradition}” rather casually. If we don’t hold the line, it will mean nothing.
Newcomers think “{tradition}” is optional. I have explained that it is not. They need to hear it from you.
I found someone doing “{tradition}” wrong. On purpose. And laughing.

choices.label: Hold the line.
choices.reaction: A reminder goes out. It is polite, firm and unexpectedly long.

choices.label: It’s all right to relax a little.
choices.reaction: Relaxing a little turns out to be very popular, which some people find worrying.

speaker: agenda:money
text: Hear me out. “{tradition}” is beloved. Beloved things can be sold. Tastefully.
variants: Hear me out. “{tradition}” is beloved. Beloved things can be sold. Tastefully.
We could charge a small fee for “{tradition}.” A suggested donation. A strongly suggested donation.
A company has offered to sponsor “{tradition}.” Their logo would be very small. Initially.

choices.label: Tastefully, then.
choices.reaction: It sells well. A purist is seen buying one, then hiding it.

choices.label: Some things aren’t for sale.
choices.reaction: {speaker} accepts this with the expression of someone filing it under “not yet.”

speaker: agenda:comfort
text: Could we have a quiet week? Everyone looks tired. I look tired. I’ve been told I always look tired, but this is different.
variants: Could we have a quiet week? Everyone looks tired. I look tired. I’ve been told I always look tired, but this is different.
I miss when it was just a few of us and the folding chairs. Can we do one {meeting} like that again?
People keep asking me what the plan is. I don’t know the plan. Is there a plan? Should there be a nap first?

choices.label: A quiet week it is.
choices.reaction: The quiet week is the most attended quiet week in history. Nobody recruits anybody. Everyone feels better.

choices.label: We keep going.
choices.reaction: Everyone keeps going. Several people keep going in their sleep.

speaker: any
text: The members in {city} feel forgotten. They say {hometown} gets all the attention and they get the leftover leaflets.
variants: The members in {city} feel forgotten. They say {hometown} gets all the attention and they get the leftover leaflets.
{city} has started doing things its own way. Nothing bad. Just different. They put the {beliefNoun} at the end instead of the start.
The {city} group has asked whether {title} might visit. They’ve already baked something. It is shaped like you.

choices.label: Visit {city} in person.
choices.reaction: You visit. They have baked something. It is, uncannily, shaped like you.

choices.label: Send a warm letter.
choices.reaction: The letter is read aloud at the {city} {meeting}, twice, and framed.

speaker: any
text: Money’s tight. The {meeting} costs more than it brings in, the coffee urn needs replacing and somebody has been buying very expensive cookies.
variants: Money’s tight. The {meeting} costs more than it brings in, the coffee urn needs replacing and somebody has been buying very expensive cookies.
We can either cut costs or raise money. Those are the options. I checked twice.

choices.label: Cut costs.
choices.reaction: Cheaper cookies are introduced. They are noticed immediately.

choices.label: Hold a fundraiser.
choices.reaction: The fundraiser involves a raffle, a bake sale and, inexplicably, a tug of war. It works.

speaker: any
text: We have money left over this month. Actual money. Nobody knows what to do with it, and everyone has a suggestion.
variants: We have money left over this month. Actual money. Nobody knows what to do with it, and everyone has a suggestion.
An anonymous donor has given us a check and a note that just says “Keep going.” What do we do with it?

choices.label: Spend it on the members.
choices.reaction: New chairs, a better coffee urn and a banner that does not sag. Morale soars.

choices.label: Train organizers with it.
choices.reaction: Two members become organizers. They are given lanyards, which they wear everywhere.

speaker: any
text: The traditionalists and the reformers have started sitting on opposite sides of the room. Nobody planned it. Now everyone knows which side is which.
variants: The traditionalists and the reformers have started sitting on opposite sides of the room. Nobody planned it. Now everyone knows which side is which.
There are now two newsletters. One says we’ve changed too much. The other says we haven’t changed enough. Both are pretty good.

choices.label: Bring them together.
choices.reaction: A joint {meeting} is held. Everyone sits in the middle, awkwardly, and it works.

choices.label: A little tension is healthy.
choices.reaction: The tension stays healthy, in the way a slowly leaking pipe is healthy.

speaker: any
text: There are {count} of us now. That number was seven not long ago. Should we mark it?

choices.label: Celebrate.
choices.reaction: There is cake, a slightly too long speech, and a photograph everyone will remember.

choices.label: Back to work.
choices.reaction: Back to work. Someone puts the number on the noticeboard anyway.

text: The {city} branch has outgrown its room. We could rent a real hall, or split into two smaller groups. The members can’t agree, so they sent me.
variants: The {city} branch has outgrown its room. We could rent a real hall, or split into two smaller groups. The members can’t agree, so they sent me.
Our {city} branch wants a budget of its own. Not much. Enough for chairs, {beliefNoun} and a banner that isn’t hand-me-down from {hometown}.
People in {city} keep asking for {title}’s opinion on local matters, such as parking. What do I tell them?

choices.label: Give {city} what it needs.
choices.reaction: The {city} branch thrives. Its newsletter thanks you by name, twice, in bold.

choices.label: {city} must make do for now.
choices.reaction: {city} makes do. Its {meeting} becomes famous for being cozy, which is a polite word for cramped.

text: I’ve run four {meetings} this week in three towns. I love this movement. I also haven’t seen my own kitchen since Tuesday.
variants: I’ve run four {meetings} this week in three towns. I love this movement. I also haven’t seen my own kitchen since Tuesday.
The organizers would like one evening a week off. We’ve made a proposal. It has a chart.

choices.label: Give the organizers real support.
choices.reaction: Organizers get a schedule, an expenses form and, crucially, an evening off. Burnout drops noticeably.

choices.label: This is what commitment looks like.
choices.reaction: The organizers keep going. One falls asleep mid-sentence and is, for once, not Gary.

speaker: any
text: The {city} branch and the {otherCity} group are feuding about whose {meeting} is more authentic. It started with a casserole.
variants: The {city} branch and the {otherCity} group are feuding about whose {meeting} is more authentic. It started with a casserole.
{city} has accused {otherCity} of copying their banner. {otherCity} says {city} copied {hometown}. {hometown} is staying out of it.

choices.label: Hold a joint {meeting}.
choices.reaction: The joint {meeting} ends with both towns agreeing that the casserole was, in fact, excellent.

choices.label: Let them compete.
choices.reaction: Both branches recruit furiously to prove a point. Neither can remember what the point was.

text: Our readers in {city} want to know what {members} actually do on a {day}. Can we send a photographer?
variants: Our readers in {city} want to know what {members} actually do on a {day}. Can we send a photographer?
We’re ranking the region’s most unusual organizations. You’re currently third, behind a choir for dogs and a man who collects traffic cones.

choices.label: Send the photographer.
choices.reaction: The photographs are mostly of Gary. Membership enquiries from {city} double.

choices.label: Politely decline.
choices.reaction: The paper runs a photograph of the outside of the building instead. It looks oddly mysterious.
